lms.title: Ethics and Trust in the Investment Profession
lms.summary: Why trust matters in finance, what makes a profession, and a framework for ethical decisions.

los.statement: Explain ethics and the role of a code of ethics in a profession.
Describe the features of a profession and the need for trust in investment management.
Distinguish between ethical and legal standards.
Describe and apply a framework for ethical decision-making.

inline.t: Ethics
is a set of moral principles that guide behaviour: deciding what is right when no one is checking. A
code of ethics
writes those principles down so that members, clients and regulators all know the standard expected.
Clients hand investment professionals their savings and cannot easily judge the quality of the advice. That information gap is why
trust
is the product the profession really sells.

items.t: and standards of conduct that members agree to follow.
: members who break the code can be disciplined.
and to serving clients and society, not just oneself.

inline.t: Imagine a dentist who says 'Trust me, that tooth has to go' and also owns the tooth-pulling franchise. You would want a code of ethics too.

items.t: : 'I am a good person, so whatever I decide must be ethical.'

inline.t: Legal is not the same as ethical.

Laws set a minimum, lag behind new products and differ between countries. Some legal acts are unethical (exploiting a loophole to mislead clients), and occasionally an ethical act can break a bad rule (whistle-blowing on fraud).
Exam questions often describe an action that is legal and ask if it is acceptable. Being legal is
not enough
; the Code and Standards may still be breached.

items.t: : the facts, the stakeholders and duties owed, the ethical principles and any conflicts of interest.
: situational influences, alternative actions, and seek guidance (compliance, a trusted colleague, the Standards).
: was the outcome as expected? What would you do differently?

inline.t: Riya, an analyst, is asked by her manager to raise a target price because the bank is pitching for the company's bond issue. Identify: duty to clients relying on the research; conflict with the banking team. Consider: pressure from her boss; options are to refuse, escalate to compliance, or disclose. Act: keep the target her analysis supports and escalate. Reflect: propose a firewall between research and banking.
The framework is a loop, not a checklist. Reflection feeds the next decision.
Ethical decision framework: Identify → Consider → Decide and act → Reflect

o: Laws often set a minimum and ethical conduct can require more

questions.e: The framework runs Identify, Consider, Decide and act, Reflect.

questions.e: Money and incentives are situational influences that can bias decisions.

questions.q: Trust is especially important in investment management mainly because:
o: Clients find it hard to judge the quality of advice they receive
questions.e: Information asymmetry means clients rely on the professional's integrity.

questions.q: In the 'Consider' step of the framework, a member would most likely:

inline.t: Disclosure fixes many conflicts, but
not
MNPI, misrepresentation or market manipulation. You cannot disclose your way out of trading on inside information.

Anil manages accounts at Moti Securities. An oversubscribed IPO is allocated to the firm. He puts shares in his own account and his brother's (a fee-paying client) before filling other clients' orders. Violations: VI(B) priority of transactions (his own account first) and III(B) fair dealing. His brother may participate only on the same terms as other clients, pro rata. Fix: a written allocation policy, pro-rata fills, and pre-clearance of personal trades.
Family accounts that are fee-paying clients must be treated like other clients: not better, and not worse.

topics.title: Case 2: the research report and the trip

inline.t: Kavya writes research on Surya Hotels. Surya offers a free week at its new resort for her family. Accepting would threaten I(B) independence and objectivity. Acceptable alternatives: decline, or have her firm pay for any genuine site visit. Separately, her report copies two charts from another broker without credit: I(C) misrepresentation (plagiarism).
A free family holiday from the company you are rating 'Buy' is the finance version of a referee accepting dinner from one team before the final.
Case method: duty owed → trigger → Standard → disclosed/consented? → procedure
